elements.text: Pilots' failure to follow established procedures for nonprecision instrument approach at night in IMC
Descent below minimum descent altitude (MDA) before required visual cues were available
Failure to adhere to the established division of duties between flying and monitoring pilots
Failure to make standard callouts
FAA regulations allowing descent below MDA into regions without assured safe obstacle clearance based only on approach lights
Failure to establish and maintain a professional demeanor during the flight
Pilot fatigue contributing to degraded performance
Low ceiling and reduced visibility at Kirksville Regional Airport making the approach more challenging
Pilots' nonessential conversation below 10,000 feet MSL contrary to sterile cockpit regulations
Cockpit environment fostering deviation from standard procedures and CRM disciplines
Pilots relying too much on minimal external visual cues instead of instruments
Captain's failure to arrest rapid descent at MDA
First officer's failure to challenge captain's descent below MDA
Use of constant-angle-of-descent approach technique instead of stabilized moderate rate-of-descent
FAA pilot duty regulations not reflecting recent research on fatigue and sleep issues
Pilots were properly certificated and qualified
Airplane was properly certificated, maintained, and equipped
No evidence of preexisting powerplant, system, or structural failure
Cargo and loading were not factors
Corporate Airlines' policies and training were consistent with industry standards
Air traffic control was not a factor
